IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: The Organizations mission is to deliver culturally competent, affordable primary medical and mental health care to low income diverse populations with a primary emphasis on the central area of the City of San Diego.
IRS990.MissionDesc: San Diego Family Care is a culturally competent, affordable, fiscally responsible and accessible primary care agency serving San Diego County by offering high quality medical care, dental care, behavioral health care, optometry care, and multicultural health promotion, with a primary focus on central San Diego.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part IV, Section B, Line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: After review by the CEO and CFO, the Form 990 is provided to each board member for review. The Form 990 is then presented to the full board and a formal vote is taken to approve the Form 990 filing. Upon board approval, the CEO signs the Form 990 and directs it to be filed on a timely basis.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Organization annually requires staff and board members to sign a written conflict of interest statement. The Organizations written conflict of interest policy details the definition of a conflict of interest. Annual in-service education is given to both the Board and staff to assure an understanding of the policy. This policy is included in the personnel manual.
During 2013, the Organization received recognition from the National Committee for Quality Assurance. The Organization is proud that they continue to maintain this recognition.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part V, Section C, Line 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy and financial statements available to the public by request through its own website.
The Organization received 124,224 for use of facilities. This amount was properly excluded for federal income tax purposes.

The Organization has a written Board approved policy regarding determination of compensation for the CEO, CFO, COO, the Chief Medical Officer as well as the two other site Medical Directors. For the CEO, the Personnel Committee fo the Board of Directors conducts a formal performance evaluation and presents local contemporaneous salary documentation to the full Board of Directors. The Board then votes for the CEO compensation.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 15b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: For the CFO, the CEO conducts a written performance evaluation and forwards the evaluation together with contemporaneous salary data for other CFOs in the local area to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. The Audit Committee votes to approve the compensation of the CFO. For the three Medical Directors and the COO, the CEO conducts a written performance evaluation annually and forwards it, with contemporaneous salary data to the Board.
